question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
trigger: User requested a harsh, last-pass first-principles Best API Review of the completed content-root locations design before execution.
requirements: Render, decoration and feature-read callbacks read the node their entry names, in the document and root where it lives; identical local paths in different roots never alias.
Paths stay root-relative and the primary root stays implicit in public API; views address their own root and Point.root is the explicit carrier (docs/vision/plite.md:307-309, 406-409).
Detached HTML/Markdown conversion stays editor-free; immutable projected documents stay read-only and source-isolated.
Static preview work stays proportional to change, per the adopted proportional-cost decision.
On next, breaking changes are allowed; order work by current shipped-user value and hard laws, not by fixture coverage.
Assessment only: no product code, plan execution, staging or publication.
evidenceReuse: Reused the design plan, its executed probe receipts (composition-current.json, summary.json) and the prior review/execution records without rerunning probes. Rechecked current source: editor-runtime-view.ts:1241-1375 (a derived view wraps its parent's fixed-root runtime; readOnly defaults false); PlateStatic.tsx:128-151 and 275-301 (block-input traversal and the contentRoot slot keep the outer editor); getPlateDecorationSources.ts:78-102 (attributes evaluated outside withDocumentViewRead); decoration-source.ts:662 (input-path fast path ignores endpoint roots); editable-text-blocks.tsx:434 with plite.tsx:272 and authored-runtime.ts:387 (automatic owned-root mounts get no inherited sources and default edit/accepted authored policy); BaseListPlugin.ts:390-402 (unresolved node fabricates listRestart/listStart/1); BaseTablePlugin.ts:1260, selection.ts:200 and context.ts:85 (presentation enters keyed selection compile; the grid itself is cached per table, so no per-cell recompilation). New census: zero content-root declarations or slots.contentRoot renders in shipped packages/platejs features, ai, lib/plugins, react or apps/www/src/registry (plugins.schema.json has 0 non-empty contentRoots); live owned/named roots appear only in Plite examples and test fixtures. Shipped callers derive views from views (PlateView.tsx:17 -> writeStaticSelectionClipboardData.ts:118-127; export-toolbar-button.tsx:161; AIChatPlugin.ts:612), and two callers already flatten to the runtime owner by hand (discussion.tsx:655, authored-fragment-view.ts:43). Ledger check passed before recording.
summary: Pursue execution; stop further design and review iterations. The selected target, the existing scoped editor with root-relative entries, is already Vision law (plite.md:406-409), so the earlier 'shared contract gap' framing overstated the problem: the defects are view-composition and delivery bugs, not a missing API. Re-rank by shipped value. S1 view derivation stays first for a stronger reason than the plan gives: shipped callers hit it (EditorPreview copy from a non-primary root with a document prop reads the projected primary root; export and AI derive views from possibly-derived editors) and two callers carry owner-flattening workarounds that S1 should delete. Known-path table and list presentation should land independently of the content-root chain; its job is the measured main-root streaming index cost (about 1.3 ms per commit for tables at CJK 50 KB), not content roots. Static content-root delivery, decoration root admission and owned-root inheritance remain small correctness repairs for a public capability no shipped Plate feature uses yet. Generalize D10: an automatic owned-root mount should inherit its owner mount's configuration in one place (decoration sources and authored policy, beside the read-only state it already inherits); today its view gets default edit/accepted authored policy unless another owner rebinds it. Narrow the S3 Find/Yjs/Code/Comments/Suggestion/AI audit to a census of sources that emit explicit or canonical roots. The 100/1,000-root cohorts measure a hypothetical explicit-view-per-root implementation, not a shipped cost; they constrain S2's implementation, not priority.

reconciliation.question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Retain Pursue, the no-carrier/no-manager cuts and the deferred caching/chunking. Correct its framing: the scoped editor already carries the root; decorations lacked correct delivery, not a root field.

reconciliation.question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Retain the target and D1-D9, D11-D18. Execution corrections: land known-path table/list presentation independently of S2/S3, widen D10 to owner-mount configuration inheritance including authored policy, delete the discussion.tsx and authored-fragment-view.ts owner-flattening workarounds in S1, census callers relying on accidental root inheritance, and narrow the S3 source audit.

reconciliation.question: Which state belongs to one document, shared root or mounted view, and can competing lifetime owners be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Flattening derivation onto the canonical runtime keeps one document runtime and independent mounted views; no lifetime owner changes.

reconciliation.question: How should list structure, numbering and indentation compose with generic block editing?
reconciliation.reason: Flat list properties and the shared ordinal algorithm stay; only target resolution and the fabricated missing-node ordinal change.

reconciliation.question: What owns table topology, cell coordinates, selection, clipboard and layout?
reconciliation.reason: Keyed grids, selection, commands and the DOM binder stay; known-path presentation reads the per-table cached pure grid.

alternatives: Iterate the design again, comparing root-bound context with root-qualified locations: Stop. Vision already fixes the location law and the design reached the same target; another pass adds no decision.

Root-qualified locations everywhere (read.ordinal({ at, root }), root fields on callbacks): Stop. It duplicates view authority while plugin and selection reads still need a coherent scoped reader; detached conversion already has its own explicit document/root/path adapter.

Delete owned content roots from Plate's public plugin surface because no shipped Plate feature declares one: Stop. contentRoots and slots.contentRoot are public, Plite multi-root and synced-block examples depend on the model, and the repairs are small once derivation is coherent. The missing shipped consumer lowers priority; it does not justify a cut.

Forbid view sources in createEditorView and require the runtime owner: Stop. It pushes document and policy re-supply onto about ten callers and still needs a validation certificate; fixing derivation at the owner deletes the existing caller workarounds instead.

Keep automatic owned-root mounts special-casing decoration sources only (D10 as written): Replace with one owner-mount inheritance rule covering sources and authored policy, because read-only, sources and authored policy currently reach the child through three different mechanisms or not at all.
Execute S1-S5 exactly as planned: Pursue with the corrections above. Keep per-block decoration caching/chunking deferred and group-last restyles as a direct Plate UI repair.
proofLimits: Source inspection plus the design's executed probes; no new probe, package test, typecheck or browser run in this review. The EditorPreview copy defect is source-traced (PlateView.tsx -> writeStaticSelectionClipboardData.ts -> createEditorView(documentView, { root })) and matches the executed probe's derivedNamed result; its user-visible effect (fallback to native copy after the rendered-text check, or the wrong node when primary-root text matches at the same path) is inferred, not reproduced. The automatic owned-root authored default is a source fact; whether it lets edits in owned roots bypass suggestion mode is unverified, because authored-fragment machinery may compensate. The decisive check is one React contract: mount an owner with authored propose/proposed, type in its owned root and assert a suggestion rather than a direct edit. The 1.3 ms per commit table index cost is the prior plan's receipt, not remeasured. The zero-consumer census covers shipped Plate package and registry source, excluding tests; custom user plugins are unobservable.
